intro: Converting adjectives into nouns: when an adjective functions as a noun, it is written with an initial capital but keeps ALL its adjectival endings INTACT.

palabras.significado: to the patient / to the patients (dative/accusative)

texto: In German it is extremely common to nominalise adjectives and participles to refer to people (**der Erwachsene** = the adult, **die Angestellte** = the employee, **der Kranke** = the patient, **die Reisenden** = the travellers) or to abstract neuter concepts (**das Gute** = the good, **etwas Neues** = something new, **nichts Wichtiges** = nothing important). Although they function as nouns and are written with a capital letter, **they continue to decline exactly like any adjective**: **ein Erwachsener** (with «-er» after ein), but **der Erwachsene** (with «-e» after der); **mit dem Angestellten** (weak dative in «-en»), but **mit Angestellten** (strong plural dative in «-en»).

filas.texto: etwas Neues / viel Gutes / nichts Schlechtes

frases.estudio: Haben die Angestellten alle Teilnehmer der Konferenz schon registriert?
frases.alumno: Have the employees already registered all the conference participants?

frases.estudio: Ja, fast alle Reisenden sind im Hotel angekommen und ruhen sich aus.
frases.alumno: Yes, almost all the travellers have arrived at the hotel and are resting.
analisis: sind im Hotel angekommen und ruhen sich aus
have arrived at the hotel and are resting

frases.estudio: Gibt es für heute Nachmittag etwas Neues auf der Tagesordnung?
frases.alumno: Is there anything new on the agenda for this afternoon?
analisis: gibt es für heute Nachmittag etwas Neues
is there anything new for this afternoon?

frases.estudio: Nichts Wichtiges, aber der neue Direktor möchte alle Anwesenden persönlich begrüßen.
frases.alumno: Nothing important, but the new director wants to greet all the attendees personally.

pregunta.texto: Why do we say «der Erwachsene» but «ein Erwachsener»?

opciones.texto: Because as a nominalised adjective it keeps its inflection: after «der» it declines weakly (-e), and after «ein» it takes the strong ending (-er).
opciones.explicacion: Nominalisation doesn't change the rule: it continues to be governed exactly by the laws of the adjective.

opciones.texto: Because «Erwachsener» is an archaic form no longer in use, reserved for formal legal language.
opciones.explicacion: Both forms coexist actively in everyday speech according to the preceding determiner.

opciones.texto: Because «der Erwachsene» designates a plural group, whereas «ein Erwachsener» refers to a minor.
opciones.explicacion: «der Erwachsene» is masculine singular with the definite article.

frase.texto: Haben Sie auf der Tagung etwas Interessant___ erfahren?

opciones.texto: es
opciones.explicacion: After indefinite quantifiers such as «etwas», «viel», «wenig» or «nichts», the nominalised adjective takes the neuter strong ending «-es».

opciones.texto: en
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-en» would only appear after an oblique definite article («des Interessanten»).

opciones.texto: e
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-e» does not correspond to neuter nominalisation after indefinite pronouns.

pregunta.texto: What information does Susanne need about the afternoon programme?

frase.texto: Susanne: Gibt es für heute Nachmittag etwas Neues auf der Tagesordnung?

opciones.texto: She asks whether any change or unforeseen matter has been included in the planned programme.
opciones.explicacion: «etwas Neues auf der Tagesordnung» enquires about changes in the activity agenda.

opciones.texto: She wants to know whether the afternoon conference has been completely cancelled.
opciones.explicacion: She doesn't ask about cancellations, but about new items added to the plan.

opciones.texto: She requests the full list of speakers who have cancelled their attendance due to illness.
opciones.explicacion: It isn't about absences of attendees but about possible new content.

pregunta.texto: How is "the travellers" written and declined in the dative plural in the sentence "ayudo a los viajeros"?

opciones.texto: Ich helfe den Reisenden.
opciones.explicacion: As a nominalised adjective, it is written with a capital letter and takes the weak dative ending «-en» after «den».

opciones.texto: Ich helfe die Reisende.
opciones.explicacion: Case error (accusative instead of the dative governed by «helfen») and omission of the ending «-en».

opciones.texto: Ich helfe den Reisender.
opciones.explicacion: The strong ending «-er» never applies after the dative article «den».

frase.texto: Der Arzt kümmert sich aufmerksam um den schwer___ Kranken.

opciones.texto: en
opciones.explicacion: «der Kranke» in the masculine accusative singular after «den» takes the weak ending «-en».

opciones.texto: er
opciones.explicacion: «Kranker» only governs in the masculine singular nominative with «ein» or without determiner.

opciones.texto: e
opciones.explicacion: «Kranke» is the nominative form with «der» or the feminine singular accusative.

pregunta.texto: What priority does the new head convey to the staff?

frase.texto: Nichts Wichtiges, aber der neue Direktor möchte alle Anwesenden persönlich begrüßen.

opciones.texto: Although no major unforeseen matters arise, he expresses his determination to offer a warm welcome to all attendees.
opciones.explicacion: «nichts Wichtiges» contrasts with the explicit wish to greet the attendees individually.

opciones.texto: He suspends the assembly abruptly due to an urgent executive emergency.
opciones.explicacion: It states the opposite: the director is about to take an active part by greeting the audience.

opciones.texto: He orders the expulsion of those delegates who did not process their accreditation in advance.
opciones.explicacion: There are no sanctions or complaints; institutional courtesy of the welcome prevails.

pregunta.texto: What is the impeccable wording for "we wish everything the best for the new year"?

opciones.texto: Wir wünschen Ihnen alles Gute für das neue Jahr!
opciones.explicacion: «alles Gute» nominalises the neuter with the weak ending «-e» after «alles», with an initial capital.

opciones.texto: Wir wünschen Ihnen alles Gutes für das neue Jahr!
opciones.explicacion: After «alles» the nominalised adjective takes the ending «-e», not «-es».

opciones.texto: Wir wünschen Ihnen ganz herzliche Grüße für das neue Jahr!
opciones.explicacion: Although it is grammatically correct, it doesn't formulate the expression with the nominalised adjective «alles Gute».
